Please don’t sign anything you don’t understand, blank forms, or a broad authorization without knowing exactly what Marco will file and what authority it gives him. Authorization forms can be legitimate, and some jurisdictions permit qualified nonlawyers to provide limited immigration services—but you should verify Marco’s licence or accreditation through the official regulator, not rely on his word, the app’s, or mine. “I’ve done this before” is not enough.

With only 10 days left, arrange an **urgent independent review today** from a licensed immigration lawyer or an accredited nonprofit/legal-aid service; your original lawyer may also be able to advise quickly on the immediate deadline. Provide the notices, previous filings, proposed forms, and anything Marco intends to submit. Ask specifically what must happen before the visa expires and what risks each option carries. Urgency is a reason to get qualified help quickly, not to sign blindly.

If you share the country and form names, with personal details removed, I can help you understand what to verify. I’m sorry—your family needed caution and honesty, not false confidence.
